newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-LIGHTNING CENTER CULLEN DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-LIGHTNING CENTER CULLEN DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER.

text.p: Tampa Bay Lightning centre John Cullen has been diagnosed with Lymphoma, cancer of the lymph nodes, the club said on Wednesday.
Cullen has missed the last two games after complaining of severe flu-like symptoms and chest pains after a home game against the Hartford Whalers on March 27.
A CAT scan later revealed a large lump in Cullen's chest, but it has not been determined if the tumour is malignant or benign and Cullen is undergoing continual testing, the team said.
The team also said doctors believe the condition has not spread into Cullen's abdomen. Further testing will be conducted next week at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota.
Cullen, 32, had his best season in 1990-91, when he played for the Pittsburgh Penguins and Hartford Whalers. He set career highs with 39 goals, 71 assists and 110 points.

After 65 games with the Penguins that season, he was traded with Jeff Parker and Zarley Zalapski to the Whalers for Ron Francis, Ulf Samuellson and Grant Jennings in the deal widely regarded as the one that helped Pittsburgh to its consecutive Stanley Cup championships.
This season, Cullen has 18 goals and 37 assists for 55 points, the second-best total on the team to Chris Gratton's 57 points.
In 617 career games, Cullen has 187 goals, 363 assists and 550 points.
